title: The Unchangeable Nature and the Life in the Trinity
english: 21. Concerning speaking of the Trinity through the unchangeable nature and essence in the holy ones. Speaking of equality in the holy ones announces the unchangeability of nature and the authority of the divine hypostases. For Zechariah—not the prophet, but the father of John—said that the Lord God of Israel has spoken through the prophets (Luke 1:57). And Paul similarly sent to the Hebrews: 'God, having spoken many times and in many ways of old to the fathers in the prophets, has spoken to us in this last age in His Son' (Hebrews 1:1-2). And to the Corinthians he wrote concerning the Son: 'since you seek the testing of the Christ speaking in me' (2 Corinthians 13:5). And the Savior according to Matthew teaches: 'for it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father is the one speaking in you' (Matthew 10:20).

22. Concerning the fact that it is written that we live by the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit through the same Word, which is the consubstantiality of the Trinity. What is written—that we live by the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit—teaches this to be seen most clearly; just as when Paul reasons with the Romans in letters: 'you consider yourselves to be dead indeed to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus our Lord' (Romans 6:11). And again: 'that those who live may no longer live for themselves, but for Him, Christ, who died for them and was raised up' (2 Corinthians 5:15); and to the Galatians: 'if we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit' (Galatians 5:25).

23. Concerning the fact that through this Word, the law from above is written to be of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Because of whom we said it is the Word, and the law from above is written to be of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, just as the Psalmist says in Psalm 40: 'the law of his God is in his heart,' and in Psalm 39: 'to do your will, O God, I have desired, and your law is in the midst of my womb' (Psalm 40:8; 39:8). And as Paul writes to the Galatians: 'one another's...'
